newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Slovak banks needn't quote to non-residents - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Slovak banks needn't quote to non-residents - CTK.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia, seeking to slow speculation by foreign investors which has put pressure on the crown currency, has told key reference banks that they need not quote crown rates to non-residents, the Czech CTK news agency reported on Thursday.
It quoted NBS spokesman Jan Onda as saying the decision came at a meeting between the central bank and executives of the large domestic banks known as reference banks.
The report did not say that the banks were prohibited from trading with non-residents. NBS officials were not available for immediate separate comment.
The Slovak and Czech crowns have for the past week been under strong speculative pressure, mainly from foreign banks.
The Czech and Slovak economies, and their currencies, remained closely linked after Czechoslovakia peacefully split into the Czech and Slovak republics in 1993.

While the Czech National Bank (CNB) has intervened several times on the market to boost the ailing currency this week, the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has used only indirect intervention through its regular fixing.

The CNB took the extraordinary steps earlier on Thursday of agreeing with large local banks to not trade with non-residents and it closed off trading in its last-resort Lombard facility, which has often been used for short selling in the Czech crown.
